```plato
//==
// # Common-ground interfaces
//
// The interfaces that mark a transform representation by the canonical form it
// converts into. Every named 2D or 3D transform reaches the general affine
// transform of its dimension (`AffineTransform2D` / `AffineTransform3D` in
// `transforms.types.plato`), so composition between representations of
// different kinds is defined by converting both sides to that common ground;
// every 3D rotation representation reaches the unit `Quaternion`, the canonical
// rotation form. A member named after a type is an implicit conversion
// (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Conversions).
//
// The interfaces narrow as they inherit: IRotational3D is a IRigid3D is an IAffine3D.
// State the narrowest one a type satisfies — a rigid transform composes and
// inverts exactly, where the affine form only promises a matrix.

// Converts to the general 2D affine transform: the common ground for composing
// 2D transforms of different kinds.
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_transformation
interface IAffine2D
{
    AffineTransform2D(x: Self): AffineTransform2D;
}
```
